title: Execution plans and analysing slow queries

videos.script: Last lesson ended on a rule. Do not add an index because it seems likely to help. Add it because you looked. This is the lesson about looking. {{rule}} Every query you send is turned into a plan before it runs. The database decides which table to read first, whether to use an index or read the whole thing, how to join, whether to sort. It writes that decision down, and it will show it to you if you ask. {{plan}} The word is EXPLAIN. Put it in front of a query and you get the plan without running anything. Put ANALYZE after it and the query runs, and beside every prediction you get what actually happened. {{explain}} That pair of numbers is the whole method. The planner said eleven rows and there were thirteen: fine. The planner said five and there were a million: that is where the query went wrong, and everything above that line inherited the mistake. {{gap}} We start before the plan, with which query to look at, because the database has been counting and the answer is rarely the one somebody guessed. {{which}} Then the plan itself. The four ways to read a table, the three ways to join two, and the lines that say whether a sort fit in memory or went to disk. {{nodes}} And a short list of what to change, in the order to try it. The first item is not an index. {{fix}}
